newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin says not to let T-bill yield rise.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin says not to let T-bill yield rise.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry said on Wednesday the current yield on treasury bills was high and that it is not prepared to allow the yield to rise further.
"The accepted yield is high, (and) we are not prepared to increase yields further," Juraj Macejka, head of the ministry's State Final Account Department, told Reuters.
Earlier on Wednesday, the average yield at an auction of four-week T-bills rose to 13.64 percent from 12.55 percent in the last auction of similar bills on December 30.
Market analysts said that if the ministry did not want to refinance the state budget deficit at rates dictated by the market, it could turn to the central bank for limited help.
"If needed, we will find some other forms (than through the central bank) to refinance the deficit," Macejka said declining to comment on the issuse further.

The state budget narrowed to 12.9 billion crowns for the first 10 months of the year, from 13.43 billion for the January-September period. The government's full-year budget target is a deficit of 27 billion crowns.
